Hold the spatial representation; do not conflate today's Thasos island geography with ancient polity extent.

activity.notes: Theagenes (also Theogenes) of Thasos was an attested ancient Greek combat-sport athlete. He won Olympic boxing at the 75th Olympiad (480 BCE) and pankration at the 76th Olympiad (476 BCE); these two events define the documented dated Activity, not his birth/death. Traditional attributions of over 1,300 or 1,400 festival victories and miracle tales about a statue belong to ancient testimony/reception, not independently verified modern sporting statistics. Distinct from Theagenes of Megara, the archaic tyrant already registered in ATLAS. Thasos was a Greek city-state, not a polity governed by Theagenes.

sources.title: International Olympic Committee — Pankration and Theagenes of Thasos
sources.citation_text: Official IOC historical account places Theagenes' boxing victory in the 75th Olympiad (480 BCE) and pankration in the 76th (476 BCE).

sources.title: Byron J. Nakamura — Boxing in the Ancient World, Cambridge Companion to Boxing
sources.citation_text: Academic account discusses Theagenes of Thasos, Pausanias, ancient Olympic victories and later hero-cult traditions.
